cues: Tenant's Proportionate Share of all Operating Expenses
versions.plain: You pay {share} of the building's costs every year, on top of your rent.

versions.example: shall not increase by more than 5% per calendar year
versions.plain: Some building costs, the ones the landlord controls, can't go up more than {percent} a year. Taxes, insurance, utilities, and snow removal usually aren't covered by the limit.

versions.example: may be carried forward to any future year
versions.plain: If costs rise less than the limit one year, the landlord can save the difference and charge more in a later year.
Your share can include the cost of major building upgrades, like a new roof.

versions.example: Landlord makes no guaranty or warranty that such estimates will be accurate
versions.plain: The building-cost amount you were quoted is only a guess. You'll pay the real amount, even if it's higher.

cues: not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed
versions.example: not to be unreasonably withheld
versions.plain: You need the landlord's permission to transfer the lease or rent out the space. The landlord needs a good reason to say no.

cues: may withhold consent for any reason
versions.plain: You need the landlord's permission to transfer the lease or rent out the space. The landlord can say no for any reason.

cues: more than fifty percent (50%) of the ownership
versions.example: change in more than fifty percent (50%) of the ownership interest
versions.plain: Selling your business, or bringing in a new owner, counts as transferring the lease. You'd need the landlord's permission.

versions.example: it shall serve to terminate the entire term of this Lease
versions.plain: If you ask to transfer the lease, the landlord can end it and take the space back instead.

versions.example: Tenant will remain primarily liable on this Lease
versions.plain: Even after you transfer the lease to a buyer, your business can still be made to pay if the buyer doesn't.

cues: pay to Landlord as Additional Rent
versions.plain: If you rent out the space for more than you pay, you must give the landlord part of the extra.

cues: shall be deemed to have consented
versions.example: Landlord shall be deemed to have consented to the proposed Transfer
versions.plain: If the landlord doesn't answer your request in time, the answer counts as yes.

versions.example: Landlord shall pay the reasonable out-of-pocket costs to relocate
versions.plain: The landlord can move your business to another space in the building, and pays the moving costs.
The landlord can move your business to another space in the building. The lease doesn't say who pays to move.

versions.plain: If you turn down the new space, your lease ends.

versions.plain: You don't have to move until the new space is finished.
